Chapter 252: The War Begins (7)
Passage 1, Demon Army Headquarters.
Every time a dimensional gate opened in the wall, the patriarchs of the Zipple clans from each dimension gathered.
However, among them, there wasn't a single 'Kelliark Zipple'. Across all dimensions, only two Kelliark Zipples remained.

Currently, sitting in the upper seat of the headquarters conference room was the Kelliark Zipple of the 33rd dimension, and the Kelliark Zipple of the 677th dimension, where the Vamel Alliance was operating.
Among them, the Kelliark of the 33rd dimension was the leader of the Unified Zipple, which encompassed all dimensions. He looked at the leaders who greeted him with a neutral expression.

The patriarchs of each dimension, in other words, the high-ranking executives of the unified Zipple, were cautiously watching his expression. The recent support mission to the 677th dimension had been proposed by the executives first.
“Lord Kelliark, everyone has arrived.”
With a gesture from Kelliark, the leaders all sat down. Most of the leaders appeared to be older, while Kelliark had an exceptionally young face.
It was like a young emperor with his ministers. The ministers bowed their heads, waiting for Kelliark’s orders.
“Yesterday, at your request, I came to the headquarters and used my power in the 677th dimension. However, the results were not particularly good.”
“Lord Kelliark, we made a mistake... Ugh, th-there!”
Crack-!
The first leader who spoke, upon meeting Kelliark’s gaze, exploded in a burst.
Then, as Kelliark gestured toward him again, a bizarre scene followed as his shattered bones and flesh reassembled themselves.
He had reversed time.

"I did not give you permission to speak yet. Delos Zipple, who just died, should be grateful that our authority has finally begun to touch upon time. If not for that, you would never have laid eyes on the world again."
“I-I’m sorry...!”
“Now, you may all speak. First, I’d like to ask how you plan to take responsibility for this. You all know very well how much power and resources are consumed by interdimensional interference."
“Lord Kelliark, it’s not necessarily a failure.”
The first to speak was Rondo Zipple. He was one of the few trusted individuals among the leaders Kelliark had called to this place.
"In what way?"
“From what we have gathered so far, Jin Runcandel, that anomali, seems to react strongly to the deaths of innocents.”
“I know that. However, slaughtering civilians is something the 677th dimension could have accomplished on its own without my help."
“But I dare say that without your power, Lord, it would not have instilled such fear. Although I cannot say it was entirely appropriate..."
“Fear, you say?”
Kelliark narrowed his eyes, cutting off Rondo’s words.

“Emotions have their limits. Whether you are an immortal or a mortal, once you overcome a certain level of fear, you can no longer be scared. Do you think the Vamel Alliance of the 677th dimension, especially Jin Runcandel, is afraid of us right now? On the contrary, they are likely burning with fighting spirit. Therefore, it will surely backfire."
His voice was filled with conviction.

As the leader of the Unified Zipple, Kelliark had experienced longer and harsher battles than anyone else in all dimensions. He had eliminated all the Kelliark from every dimension except the 677th, and had claimed the throne of the Unified Zipple alone.

“Furthermore, such will sometimes leads to miracles. That is why the powerhouses of the 677th dimension have so far failed to kill the anomaly named Jin Runcandel. The Vamel Alliance is a powerful enemy, the likes of which no other dimension has ever faced."
“My thinking was short-sighted.”

“Since we dominate all dimensions except for the 677th, and since we possess the completed Origin Stone, everyone believes we will be able to eliminate them. But that’s wrong. Their swords are already at our neck.”
It wasn’t an exaggeration. Kelliark, the leader of the Unified Zipple, truly believed this.
“To safely and completely subdue them, we have only two options.”
“...May I ask what they are?”

“The first is to secure the complete resurrection of the Sun God through a dimension where the possibility still remains. With that power, we will be able to control time, our final desire. The second is to gather all possible power and resources and begin a powerful interference in the 677th dimension as quickly as possible."
The leaders’ eyes widened.
The resurrection and securing of the Sun God was a major objective that had been set from the beginning, but 'forced interference' was something not in the plan at all.

“And I will execute the second plan, starting today. There must never again be a case of ambiguous support leading to a clumsy result like this time. If this kind of thing repeats a few times, it is clear that at some point, they will develop to a level where they can truly challenge us."
Perhaps they are pouring too much into one dimension.
No one dared to speak up against that. The Kelliark of the 33rd dimension was, after all, the leader of the Unified Zipple and the sole ruler of all dimensions, except for the 677th.

“Of course, just by carrying out a direct intervention, we are likely to lose a lot of power and resources. But if we just clean up the 677th, nothing can threaten us. The lost power and resources can be restored at any time."
Kelliark’s gaze once again fell on Rondo Zipple.
“...What should we prepare first?”

“First, we need a way for the Demon Army to directly enter. Once they establish a foothold in the 677th dimension, I will personally enter the battle as well. Also, gather all the powerhouses from each dimension who can withstand the aftereffects of dimensional infiltration to the headquarters. We will begin an all-out war."
677th Dimension, The Tower of Stories.
Kelliark sat, looking at Elona, who was rooted like a tree at the lower part of the Origin Stone. He knew that someone would soon appear before him.
"You've come, Lokia Ganesto."
Lokia Ganesto, she had come to Kelliark in the form of Hailyn Runcandel, just as she had during the Lafrarosa Liberation War.
"Kelliark Zipple, I heard you got your ass kicked by my descendant. Well, I also got completely torn apart by Jin in Lafrarosa."

"To not only find this tower, which even the Vamel Alliance cannot easily track, in one go, but to also enter its very core directly. Your skills are unusual. It doesn't seem to be chaos, so you must be able to use the power of the Sun God to a fairly high level."
"It's not a level that can be compared to you lot, who didn't even know Elona Zipple, Malugia, was right under your noses."
"What brings you here?"
"Isn't it obvious? A deal. I have the only card that can prolong your lives, you who are like a candle in the wind."
"Haha..."

"Don't laugh, you son of a bitch. Do you... possibly think I came here because I feel sorry for you? You Zipples are pests that should have all died a thousand years ago. The only thing you've done since you were born is ruin this world."
Lokia stared at Kelliark with a broad grin. Despite the sudden outburst of insults, Kelliark maintained a calm demeanor.
But in truth, he was feeling uneasy. The calculations were continuously off by a little, and the fact that Lokia had entered this place, ignoring all its defenses, was also shocking.

Moreover, just like others who had come to learn the truth of the world, he had only recently recognized the existence of multiple dimensions. This realization came as the Demon Army began to indirectly support the Zipple of this world.

“You wouldn't think that I'm unaware of the multiple dimensions that Orgal, the Vamel Alliance, and even you now know about, would you? And you don't want to die. At least not right now. Not to the Vamel Alliance, not to me, and not to the unified Zipple."
"I admit your abilities caught me of guard. But if you could kill me, why not just threaten me instead of spouting all this noise? Threaten to kill me if I don't accept your proposal."
"Yeah, I was just about to do that."
Biiing...!

Suddenly, Kelliark was enveloped by a ringing in his ears so intense it felt like his head was about to shatter. He didn’t know what it was, but it was clearly Lokia’s trick. Just as he was about to retaliate, Kelliark swiftly turned and looked toward the Origin Stone. A tremendous amount of Sun Energy was being emitted from it.
To be exact, it wasn’t from the Origin Stone itself but from Elona Zipple’s body, which had merged with it. And that energy was resonating with Lokia.
As if a single person was wielding the power, as if they had been one from the beginning.
Kelliark urgently tried to control the Origin Stone, but it was futile. In fact, it seemed that the Origin Stone was reacting more strongly to Lokia’s will.
"You probably don't understand what's happening right now, do you, Kelliark."
"...What is it?"

"Malugia, she is the largest ego among the wills of destruction that split off from the Sun God. And the being dwelling within the owner of this body, my niece... Hailyn Runcandel, is also an ego of Destruction called Araxion. For your information, those two are very close."

This was the reason Lokia could easily enter the deepest part of the Tower of Stories, right before the Origin Stone. Like magnets being drawn to each other, egos with the same will were naturally bound to connect. No matter where they were.

“It's disconcerting, isn't it, to suddenly lose control of the Origin Stone? Do you really think it would be difficult for me to awaken Malugia and ruin the Origin Stone? As long as you are attached to the stone, I can find you wherever you are... and finish you at any time."
From Kelliark’s perspective, he couldn’t discern the truth of Lokia’s words.
This was because he couldn't gain insight into Lokia even with the divinity he obtained by fusing with Shinu, nor could he control the Origin Stone

However, one thing was clear. Even if there were some exaggeration in what Lokia said, she was undoubtedly an extremely dangerous being. The possibility of someone interfering with the Origin Stone’s power in this way had never even crossed his mind.
In the end, Kelliark had no choice but to answer her like this.
“…What do you want from me, Lokia Ganesto?”
